project_context: HL-GA Battery Company LLC (Hyundai Motor Group + LG Energy Solution EV battery cell joint venture), Ellabell, Bryan County, Georgia, USA; adjacent to Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America.
risk_cause__value: DHS/ICE conducted its largest-ever single-site worksite enforcement operation at the HL-GA site on 2025-09-04, detaining ~475 workers (300+ South Korean nationals), most performing specialized equipment installation/commissioning work.
delay_description_value: Hyundai CEO Jose Munoz's own quoted estimate (2025-09-11); actual plant opening occurred April 2026, consistent with a multi-month slip though the exact pre-raid baseline target date is disputed across sources.
response_value: Hyundai/LG did not cancel or scale back the project; Hyundai separately announced continuation of a $2.7B expansion of the wider Georgia complex despite the raid. The facility was reported physically complete Dec 2025 and opened April 2026 with 500+ employees.
exclusion_notes: None for this case's included metrics; original pre-raid target date is disputed across sources (see source_conflicts), which limits delay_MAE to partially_usable rather than usable.

project_context: Micron Clay Megafab (Fab 1 of a planned multi-fab campus), Clay, New York (Onondaga County), USA.
risk_cause__value: Micron's Final Environmental Impact Statement (released Nov 2025) disclosed the first Clay fab's construction would be delayed; Onondaga County Executive Ryan McMahon attributed it to 'longer construction cycles and labor shortages' (one local report additionally cites 'labor and supply chain issues').
affected_tasks: Concrete pouring and foundation work for Fab 1 (postponed to Q2 2026) [OBSERVED/S002] | Site clearing/grading for the broader campus (continues on original 2025 schedule) [OBSERVED/S002]
delay_description_value: First fab opening shifted from mid/late-2028 to 2030 (Q3 2030 per some outlets); directly attributed to a named county official and the project's own Final EIS document, corroborated across 5 independent outlets.
response_value: Site-clearing and grading work for the wider campus continues in 2025 on schedule even though concrete/foundation work for Fab 1 specifically is deferred to Q2 2026 -- a phased, partial-continuation response rather than a full project halt.
exclusion_notes: None; this is one of the strongest cases in the dataset.

project_context: Samsung Austin Semiconductor fab (operating facility), Austin, Texas, USA.
risk_cause__value: Winter Storm Uri (Feb 2021) caused a Texas grid emergency; Austin Energy forced an emergency shutdown of major electricity users including Samsung's Austin fab to preserve power for homes and hospitals.
affected_tasks: Ongoing wafer production/output at the operating fab (not a construction WBS milestone) [OBSERVED/S003]
delay_description_value: Samsung spokesperson statement (2021-03-30) said the fab had 'reached production close to normal levels... as of last week'; the '~6 weeks' figure is an INFERRED calculation (statement date minus storm date), since no exact day-count was directly quoted. Full normalization was separately stated by Samsung as occurring within Q2 2021.
response_value: Phased equipment inspection, reconfiguration, and restart, per Samsung's own public statement ('efforts to resume operations... inspect and reconfigure the facility'). No more granular technical mitigation plan was found.
exclusion_notes: affected_task_retrieval and response_evaluation are partially_usable only: this is an operating-facility production disruption, not a construction-project WBS milestone, and the response detail found is general rather than granular.

project_context: Rivian Georgia EV Plant (Stanton Springs North), Social Circle / Rutledge, Georgia, USA.
risk_category__value: contractor/construction (true driver: financial/capital-allocation decision, not a clean fit to the 8-category taxonomy)
risk_cause__value: Rivian paused construction in March 2024 to conserve capital, shifting planned R2 model production to its existing Normal, Illinois plant instead.
affected_tasks: Coarse-level only: pre-construction site work vs. vertical construction vs. production -- NOT usable at fine WBS-task granularity, since 'pause -> loan finalized (Jan 2025) -> ceremonial groundbreaking (Sep 2025) -> site grading -> vertical construction (2026) -> production (late 2028)' spans 5+ imprecisely-dated, overlapping milestones. [INFERRED/S004]
delay_description_value: No source states one authoritative delay figure. A defensible range: ~18 months (pause to ceremonial groundbreaking) or ~2+ years (pause to actual vertical construction), but this is an INFERRED range, not an OBSERVED single value.
response_value: Rivian secured, then later restructured, DOE financing ($6.6B conditional commitment Jan 2025, later 'up to $4.5B'); separately announced an 'optimized capacity plan' raising planned annual capacity from 200,000 to 300,000 vehicles.
exclusion_notes: affected_task_retrieval and delay_MAE are NOT_USABLE: the 'restart' is defined differently across at least 5 overlapping, imprecisely-dated milestones, and the DOE loan amount itself is reported inconsistently over time. Usable only for risk_classification (partial), evidence_retrieval, and response_evaluation (partial).

project_context: Renesas Naka Factory, N3 building (300mm automotive-chip production line), Hitachinaka, Ibaraki Prefecture, Japan.
risk_category__value: equipment (industrial fire; not a clean fit to the 8-category taxonomy)
risk_cause__value: Overcurrent ignition in plating equipment (casing/tank materials with low heat resistance) started a fire at 02:47 JST on 2021-03-19, extinguished by 08:12 JST the same day; damaged ~2% of the fab's manufacturing equipment (~600 sq m, ~5% of the cleanroom).
affected_tasks: N3 building's 300mm production line specifically (not the whole factory) [OBSERVED/S005]
delay_description_value: 29 days fire-to-partial-restart (<10% of pre-fire capacity, 2021-03-19 to 2021-04-17); 97 days fire-to-100%-production (2021-03-19 to 2021-06-24); ~18 weeks to expected shipment-level normalization (3rd week of July 2021). All three figures sourced directly to Renesas's own numbered official updates, independently corroborated by Bloomberg and Embedded Computing Design.
cost_value: approximately 17 billion yen (~$156 million) per month
response_value: Renesas published a sequential, numbered public disclosure series (UPDATE 1 through at least UPDATE 10) tracking capacity restoration in stages; pursued an expedited equipment-replacement/requalification effort as the substantive recovery action.
exclusion_notes: None; this is the best-documented case in the dataset (official company source with a full day-by-day recovery curve).

risk_cause__value: TSMC announced (2023-07-20) it would delay N4-process production at its first Arizona fab from a late-2024 target to 2025, citing a shortage of skilled specialized construction/installation labor.
affected_tasks: Coarse level only (production-start milestone); fine WBS-task-level attribution not established. [INFERRED/S006]
delay_description_value: The 12-month figure is the ANNOUNCED delay per the 2023 Bloomberg report (late-2024 to 2025), not a confirmed realized outcome: TSMC's own official webpage claims high-volume production 'started in Q4 2024' (matching the ORIGINAL pre-delay target), while a dated 2024-12-13 CNBC report describes the fab as still in pilot/sample-wafer production at that time. This conflict is UNRESOLVED (see source_conflicts) -- marked INFERRED rather than OBSERVED for this reason.
response_value: TSMC hired 900+ local workers by Q1 2023, sent experienced Taiwanese technicians to train local staff, and later reached a project labor agreement with the Arizona Building and Construction Trades Council.
exclusion_notes: delay_MAE is NOT_USABLE: the core numeric delay claim is contested by unresolved conflicting primary-source vs. press evidence about whether the delay was actually realized in final output timing.

project_context: General Motors North American assembly plants (Fort Wayne IN, Silao Mexico, Wentzville MO) -- April 2021 shutdown wave.
risk_cause__value: The global semiconductor shortage forced GM to pause production at Fort Wayne, Silao, and Wentzville per GM's 2021-04-08 announcement, attributed to 'continued parts shortages caused by semiconductor supply constraints from international markets experiencing COVID-19-related restrictions.'
affected_tasks: Silverado/Sierra HD truck line (Fort Wayne, Silao) [OBSERVED/S007] | Midsize truck and full-size van lines (Wentzville) [OBSERVED/S007]
delay_description_value: Fort Wayne and Silao paused 1 week; Wentzville paused 2 weeks, per GM's dated announcement, cross-confirmed via Washington Post, CNBC, and WANE 15.
cost_value: $1.5-2 billion (company-wide 2021 operating profit impact from the broader chip shortage)
response_value: GM prioritized available semiconductor supply toward its most profitable/high-demand vehicles; no finer-grained mitigation detail was found.
exclusion_notes: response_evaluation is partially_usable only: the response is a general strategy statement, not a granular mitigation plan. Note also this event was part of a chronic, recurring 2021 disruption pattern (repeat waves in July and September), not a single isolated event -- see source_conflicts.

project_context: Ford Kansas City Assembly Plant (Claycomo, Missouri), USA -- F-150 / Transit production.
risk_cause__value: The global semiconductor shortage forced Ford to halt F-150 and Transit van production at its Kansas City plant, per Ford's own statement: 'The global semiconductor shortage continues to affect global automakers and other industries in all parts of the world.'
affected_tasks: F-150 pickup line [OBSERVED/S008] | Transit cargo van line [OBSERVED/S008]
delay_description_value: Plant halted production for 2 weeks starting May 17, 2021; halted again starting July 12, 2021 (F-150, 2 weeks) and July 19, 2021 (Transit, 1 week), corroborated across WHAS11, Fox4KC, and CBS News.
response_value: Ford prioritized completing partially-assembled vehicles awaiting missing chip-dependent parts rather than halting all output; no more specific chip-allocation strategy for this plant was found.
exclusion_notes: response_evaluation is partially_usable only: response detail found is general, not plant-specific. IMPORTANT: this case corrects a STEP 1 error (L3-017) that had wrongly merged this US event with a German event (see V3-004 / source_conflicts).

project_context: Ford Saarlouis Assembly Plant (Ford Focus production line), Saarlouis, Saarland, Germany.
risk_cause__value: The global semiconductor shortage forced Ford to idle its Saarlouis, Germany plant (Focus production, ~6,200 workers) from January 18 to February 19, 2021.
delay_description_value: Production halted Jan 18 - Feb 19, 2021 (32 days), directly dated and corroborated across at least 4 independent outlets (Bloomberg, CNN, fordauthority.com, Nasdaq/Reuters).
exclusion_notes: response_evaluation is NOT_USABLE: no plant-specific mitigation action was found in the sources reviewed (Ford's broader US chip-prioritization strategy was not tied to Saarlouis specifically). This case is a NEW record split out of STEP 1's flawed L3-017 (which incorrectly labeled this German event's country as 'USA').

project_context: VinFast Manufacturing US LLC plant, Chatham County 'Moncure megasite', North Carolina, USA.
risk_category__value: regulation/permitting, compounded with contractual default / financial (capital-allocation) factors
risk_cause__value: VinFast's Chatham County plant, promised March 2022 (7,500 jobs, 2024 production), stalled after clearing trees in 2023 and ceasing further work by December 2024, citing a global EV sales slowdown affecting financing.
affected_tasks: Site was cleared of trees in 2023 (early WBS-equivalent stage); no further construction occurred after December 2024 -- the project stalled between 'site clearing' and 'vertical construction' and never resumed. [OBSERVED/S010]
delay_description_value: Not usable as a single delay figure: the project's status changed from 'delayed' to 'terminated/defaulted' -- Chatham County formally terminated its incentive agreement (2026-07-27) and the State of North Carolina sued to reclaim the site (2026-05-21), a different outcome category than a completed-but-late project.
response_value: VinFast repeatedly requested schedule extensions (first 2024-05-10, citing a global EV sales slowdown affecting its financing) and ultimately proposed a drastically scaled-back project (from 7,500 to approximately 1,400 jobs) rather than completing the original plan.
exclusion_notes: delay_MAE is NOT_USABLE: the project outcome is contract termination/legal dispute, not a late-but-completed project, so there is no well-defined 'delay in days' to measure. Usable for risk_classification (partial), affected_task_retrieval, evidence_retrieval, and response_evaluation.

project_context: CATL Debrecen Battery Plant (cell-production lines), Debrecen, Hungary.
risk_cause__value: Hungary's withdrawal of the streamlined 'key investment project' permitting exemption, plus a nickel-dust occupational-safety incident that triggered a temporary suspension of CATL's Debrecen cell-production lines.
affected_tasks: Cell-production lines specifically, distinct from the module-assembly plant (which had already been producing since May 2026) [OBSERVED/S011]
delay_description_value: From the 'early 2026' target (S&P Global Autotech Insight) to confirmed trial-production start on 2026-09-22 (multi-source confirmed). This is a delay to the TRIAL milestone, not to full mass production, which remains unscheduled; the exact delay length is INFERRED since 'early 2026' is an approximate target window.
response_value: CATL secured 'all permits required for trial operations' before starting; was separately required to complete rectifications of occupational-safety deficiencies (the nickel-dust exposure incident) as a precondition.
exclusion_notes: delay_MAE is partially_usable only (delay to trial milestone, not mass production, and the original target is an approximate window not an exact date). This is the closest real-world match found to the original service brief's Hungary regulation example.

project_context: Intel Ohio One (New Albany, Ohio) semiconductor fabs, USA.
risk_category__value: regulation/policy & funding uncertainty (no clean fit in the 8-category taxonomy)
risk_cause__value: Intel's Ohio One fabs, originally targeted to begin production in 2025 when the $28B investment was announced in 2022, were repeatedly restated -- confirmed via Intel's own official newsroom page -- citing CHIPS Act funding uncertainty and market conditions.
affected_tasks: Site/foundation work (6.4M work-hours, 200,000+ cubic yards of concrete, sub-utility trenches complete, 'go vertical' milestone achieved with below-grade structure complete and above-ground structure underway) [OBSERVED/S012]
delay_description_value: Original 2025 target -> current ~2030 Mod 1 operations target (per Intel's own newsroom, Mod 1 operations 2030-2031, Mod 2 operations 2032). This is a compounding SEQUENCE of at least 3 separate delay announcements over 3 years (2022 target, a 2024 delay, the Feb 2025 delay to 2030), so the cumulative '~5 years' figure is an INFERRED sum, not one OBSERVED single-event figure.
response_value: Construction continues (not halted) at a deliberately slower pace; Intel's own statement: 'taking a prudent approach to ensure we complete the project in a financially responsible manner' (EVP Naga Chandrasekaran).
exclusion_notes: risk_classification and delay_MAE are partially_usable only: this is a compounding, multi-cause, repeatedly-restated delay rather than one clean event -> one impact story, and the category does not map cleanly to the 8-category taxonomy.
